```{r setupDocument, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

## Goal
Analyze silencing elements to assess how likely these are to be true distal regulatory elements.
```{r attachPackages}
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
library(cowplot)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)
```

```{r generalParams}
# colors for interaction classes
class_colors <- c(enhancer = "steelblue", silencer = "red3")
```


***

## Used data
Annotated CRE screen results are used as main input for these analyses. Only enhancer-like CRE-gene
interactions are used, since these are a confident list of CRE-gene regulatory interactions. 
```{r loadMainData}
# load annotated main results table
etp <- fread(snakemake@input$annot_pairs)

# for control perturbations which were in multiple panels, select the most significant one
etp_ctrl <- etp %>% 
  filter(ctrl_perturbation == TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(response_id, grna_target) %>% 
  slice_min(p_value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

# add back to results table with discovery pairs
etp <- etp %>% 
  filter(ctrl_perturbation == FALSE) %>% 
  bind_rows(etp_ctrl) %>% 
  arrange(desc(p_value))

# add pseudocount to Hi-C interaction frequencies
etp <- mutate(etp, hic_int_freq = hic_int_freq + 1)

# filter out any trans-chromosomal interactions
etp <- filter(etp, pert_chr == gene_chr)

# extract significant hits to analyze
sig_distal_hits <- etp %>% 
  filter(enhancer_like_interaction) %>% 
  filter(abs(dist_to_tss) <= 1e6)

# add effect direction and unique identifier for each pair
sig_distal_hits <- sig_distal_hits %>% 
  mutate(int_class = if_else(log_2_fold_change <= 0, true = "enhancer", false = "silencer")) %>% 
  group_by(grna_target) %>% 
  mutate(elem_class = case_when(
    all(int_class == "enhancer") ~ "enhancer",
    all(int_class == "silencer") ~ "silencer",
    TRUE ~ "bidirectional"
  )) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  unite(col = "pair_uid", grna_target, response_id, sep = "|", remove = FALSE)
```

***

## Effect direction as function of distance to TSS
Plot effect sizes as well as percentage of silencers (up-regulation upon perturbation) elements as
function of distance to TSS.
```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=3.5}
# make distance to tss bin an ordered factor
all_bins <- c("1500-10k", "10k-100k", "100k-1Mb")
sig_distal_hits <- sig_distal_hits %>% 
  mutate(distToTSS_bin = factor(distToTSS_bin, levels = all_bins, ordered = TRUE))

# calculate proportion of element class per distance bin
prop_int_class_dist <- sig_distal_hits %>% 
  count(distToTSS_bin, int_class) %>%
  group_by(distToTSS_bin) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

# plot effect sizes as function of distance to TSS
p1 <- ggplot(sig_distal_hits, aes(x = dist_to_tss, y = log_2_fold_change, color = int_class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1e4, 1e5, 1e6), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Effect size vs. distance", x = "Distance to TSS (bp)", y = "Log2 fold change",
       color = "Interaction class") +
  scale_color_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  geom_point() +
  theme_classic()

# plot the proportion of silencers as funcion of distance to TSS (bins)
p2 <- ggplot(prop_int_class_dist, aes(x = distToTSS_bin, y = prop, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Proportion effect direction", x = "Distance to TSS (bin)",
       y = "Proportion of CRE-gene interactions", fill = "Interaction class") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  theme_classic()

# arrange into one figure
plot_grid(p1, p2, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 0.75))
```

Overall `r round(mean(sig_distal_hits$int_class == "silencer") * 100, digits = 2)` of CRE-gene
interactions within 1Mb are "silencers". The proportion of silencing interactions increase as a
function of distance to TSS, which is in line with previous work (e.g. Ray et al., 2025).

To verify this, let's repeat the same analysis with the Ray et al., 2025 dataset:
```{r}
# load main results table and filter for significant distal element-gene interactions
ray_sig_distal <- fread(snakemake@input$ray2025_results) %>% 
  filter(DistalElement_Gene == TRUE, significant_wo_pos_controls_20fdr == TRUE)

# bin hits by distance to TSS
ray_sig_distal <- ray_sig_distal %>% 
    mutate(distToTSS_bin = case_when(
      distance_to_abc_canonical_TSS <= 1e4 ~ "<10k",
      distance_to_abc_canonical_TSS <= 1e5 ~ "10k-100k",
      distance_to_abc_canonical_TSS <= 1e6 ~ "100k-1Mb",
      TRUE ~ ">1Mb"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(distToTSS_bin = factor(distToTSS_bin, levels = c("<10k", "10k-100k", "100k-1Mb", ">1Mb"),
                                ordered = TRUE))

# add interaction class
ray_sig_distal <- ray_sig_distal %>% 
  mutate(int_class = if_else(log_2_FC_effect_size <= 0, true = "enhancer", false = "silencer"))

# calculate proportion of element class per distance bin
ray_prop_int_class_dist <- ray_sig_distal %>% 
  count(cell_type, distToTSS_bin, int_class) %>%
  group_by(cell_type, distToTSS_bin) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

# only retain the same distance bins as in our data
ray_prop_plot <- filter(ray_prop_int_class_dist, distToTSS_bin != ">1Mb")

# plot the proportion of element class as function of distance to TSS (bin)
ggplot(ray_prop_plot, aes(x = distToTSS_bin, y = prop, fill = int_class)) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_type) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Proportion effect direction Ray et al., 2025", x = "Distance to TSS (bin)",
       y = "Proportion of CRE-gene interactions", fill = "Interaction class") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```
Rates of "silencer" CRE-gene interactions are even higher in this screen. This might be driven by
the random screen designs of this study and the paper argues that distal regulatory interactions
are more likely to be the results of indirect effects. This might apply to our dataset as well and
we should discuss this.

As a third dataset, let's compare it to the K562 enhancer perturbation "gold-standard" dataset from
Gasperini et al., 2019.
```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=3.5}
# load ENCODE processed CRISPR data and extract Gasperini data. Caveats: this is from our own
# processing, which is similar to this screen but isn't the published version.
gasp <- fread(snakemake@input$gasperini2019_results)

# filter for significant distal hits within 1Mb 
gasp_sig <- gasp %>% 
  filter(Significant == TRUE, !is.na(EffectSize)) %>% 
  filter(abs(distToTSS) > 1500, abs(distToTSS) <= 1e6) %>% 
  filter(ValidConnection == "TRUE")  # filters out any promoter promoter and own target gene overlap

# convert log fold change to log2 fold change
gasp_sig <- mutate(gasp_sig, log_2_fold_change = EffectSize / log(2))

# bin hits by distance to TSS
gasp_sig <- gasp_sig %>% 
    mutate(distToTSS_bin = case_when(
      abs(distToTSS) <= 1e4 ~ "<10k",
      abs(distToTSS) <= 1e5 ~ "10k-100k",
      abs(distToTSS) <= 1e6 ~ "100k-1Mb",
      TRUE ~ ">1Mb"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(distToTSS_bin = factor(distToTSS_bin, levels = c("<10k", "10k-100k", "100k-1Mb", ">1Mb"),
                                ordered = TRUE))

# add interaction class
gasp_sig <- gasp_sig %>% 
  mutate(int_class = if_else(EffectSize <= 0, true = "enhancer", false = "silencer"))

# calculate proportion of element class per distance bin
gasp_prop <- gasp_sig %>% 
  count(distToTSS_bin, int_class) %>%
  group_by(distToTSS_bin) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

# plot effect sizes as function of distance to TSS
p1 <- ggplot(gasp_sig, aes(x = abs(distToTSS), y = log_2_fold_change, color = int_class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1e4, 1e5, 1e6), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Effect size vs. distance", x = "Distance to TSS (bp)", y = "Log2 fold change",
       color = "Interaction class") +
  scale_color_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  geom_point() +
  theme_classic()

# plot the proportion of element class as function of distance to TSS (bin)
p2 <- ggplot(gasp_prop, aes(x = distToTSS_bin, y = prop, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Proportion effect direction Gasperini et al., 2019", x = "Distance to TSS (bin)",
       y = "Proportion of CRE-gene interactions", fill = "Interaction class") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())

# arrange into one figure
plot_grid(p1, p2, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 0.75))
```

Although the Gasperini et al., 2019 dataset does not have as many silencers close to the TSS, it has
comparable numbers of silencer-like interactions beyond 100kb. This is again in line with the
higher proportion of indirect effects at longer ranges assumption. Note that Gasperini et al.,
applied stronger prioritization for enhancer chromatin states that us, potentially reducing the
number of tested silencer elements. 

As a last piece, let's calculate the expected baseline rate of positive effects on expression from 
indirect, not CRE-mediated effects, from trans-chromosome tests.
```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=3}
# load all tested pairs, including trans-acting interactions
all_pairs <- fread(snakemake@input$all_pairs)

# filter for significant trans-chromosome pairs involving distal elements
all_sig_trans_pairs <- all_pairs %>% 
  filter(significant == TRUE, pert_chr != gene_chr, element_type == "intergenic") %>% 
  mutate(int_class = if_else(log_2_fold_change <= 0, true = "enhancer", false = "silencer"))

# calculate proportion of silencers and enhancers
sig_trans_prop <- all_sig_trans_pairs %>% 
  count(int_class) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>% 
  mutate(distToTSS_bin = "trans-chrom.")

# plot proportion silencer- and enhancer-like effects in significant trans-chromosome interactions
ggplot(sig_trans_prop, aes(x = distToTSS_bin, y = prop, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  labs(title = "Trans-chrom. effects", y = "Proportion of CRE-gene interactions",
       fill = "Interaction class") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank())
```


***

## Chromatin properties
Explore various chromatin properties of silencer-like vs. enhancer-like elements.

### Distance to target genes
Compare distance to TSS between silencer-like and enhancer-like interactions:
```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# plot distance to TSS distributions
ggplot(sig_distal_hits, aes(x = int_class, y = abs(dist_to_tss) / 1000, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
  labs(title = "Distance to TSS", y = "Distance to TSS (kb)", x = "Interaction class") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

This highlights the findings from above, showing that silencer-like elements tend to be further away
from the target gene TSS (more likely indirect effects).

### Chromatin landscape

Next let's look at chromating marks of silencer-like elements vs. enhancer-like elements:
```{r, fig.height=7, fig.width=7}
# extract and reformat chromatin assays at enhancers for plots
sig_distal_hits_chrom <- sig_distal_hits %>% 
  select(pair_uid, int_class, `enh_signal_avg_DNase-seq`, enh_signal_avg_H3K27ac,
         enh_signal_avg_H3K4me1, enh_signal_avg_H3K9me3, enh_signal_avg_H3K27me3,
         enh_signal_avg_CTCF, tss_signal_avg_H3K4me3, `tss_signal_avg_DNase-seq`) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(pair_uid, int_class), values_to = "signal", names_to = "measurement") %>% 
  mutate(measurement = sub("signal_avg_", "", measurement))

# plot chromatin assay signal for enhancers vs silencers
ggplot(sig_distal_hits_chrom, aes(x = int_class, y = signal, fill = int_class)) +
  facet_wrap(~ measurement, scales = "free") +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
  labs(x = "Interaction class", y = "FC over control", title = "Chromatin assays") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.background = element_blank())
```

Only H3K27ac, a typical enhancer mark, seems decreased at silencer-like elements. While low H3K27ac
has been observed at silencers, this by itself is not strong evidence that these are real silencers,
since this could also be a sign that these simply false positives that aren't CREs at all.

To separate these two possibilities, let's look at accessibility and H3K27ac jointly. Elements that
are accessible but lack H3K27ac are plausible real silencers, while elements low in both assays are
more likely not CREs at all.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
# accessibility vs. active enhancer mark at each perturbed element
enh_signal <- sig_distal_hits %>%
  select(pair_uid, int_class, dnase = `enh_signal_avg_DNase-seq`,
         h3k27ac = enh_signal_avg_H3K27ac, ctcf = enh_signal_avg_CTCF) %>%
  drop_na(dnase, h3k27ac)

# scatter plot of DNase-seq vs H3K27ac signal, colored by interaction class. A pseudocount of 1 is
# added since some elements have no signal in either assay. The legend is dropped when assembling
# the figure so that the main panel aligns with the marginal plots, and is added back at the end
p_enh_signal <- ggplot(enh_signal, aes(x = h3k27ac + 1, y = dnase + 1, color = int_class)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Accessibility vs. H3K27ac at perturbed elements",
       x = "H3K27ac (FC over control + 1)", y = "DNase-seq (FC over control + 1)",
       color = "Interaction class") +
  scale_color_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic()

# axis_canvas() inherits the main panel's ranges in transformed (log10) space with an identity
# transform, so marginal layers need to be passed pre-transformed values. Boxplots additionally
# need a numeric class position, since the canvas y scale is continuous
marg_data <- enh_signal %>%
  mutate(log_h3k27ac = log10(h3k27ac + 1),
         log_dnase = log10(dnase + 1),
         class_pos = as.numeric(factor(int_class)))

# build one density and one boxplot canvas for a given margin
marginal_grobs <- function(plot, signal, axis) {
  flip <- axis == "y"
  dens <- axis_canvas(plot, axis = axis, coord_flip = flip) +
    geom_density(data = marg_data, aes(x = .data[[signal]], color = int_class, fill = int_class),
                 alpha = 0.4) +
    scale_color_manual(values = class_colors) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors)
  box <- axis_canvas(plot, axis = axis, coord_flip = flip) +
    geom_boxplot(data = marg_data,
                 aes(x = .data[[signal]], y = class_pos, group = int_class, fill = int_class),
                 orientation = "y", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.3, outlier.size = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors)
  if (flip) list(dens = dens + coord_flip(), box = box + coord_flip())
  else list(dens = dens, box = box)
}

x_marg <- marginal_grobs(p_enh_signal, "log_h3k27ac", axis = "x")
y_marg <- marginal_grobs(p_enh_signal, "log_dnase", axis = "y")

# assemble figure, with densities next to the main panel and boxplots outside of them
p_marg <- p_enh_signal + theme(legend.position = "none")
p_marg <- insert_xaxis_grob(p_marg, x_marg$dens, unit(0.2, "null"), position = "top")
p_marg <- insert_xaxis_grob(p_marg, x_marg$box, unit(0.12, "null"), position = "top")
p_marg <- insert_yaxis_grob(p_marg, y_marg$dens, unit(0.2, "null"), position = "right")
p_marg <- insert_yaxis_grob(p_marg, y_marg$box, unit(0.12, "null"), position = "right")

# add the legend back next to the assembled figure
plot_grid(ggdraw(p_marg), get_legend(p_enh_signal), nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 0.25))
```

The marginal distributions show that silencer-like elements are shifted towards lower H3K27ac,
while their accessibility distribution largely overlaps with that of enhancer-like elements. Most
silencer-like elements are therefore accessible but depleted of H3K27ac, rather than being
inaccessible regions that are unlikely to be CREs at all.

A simpler way to look at the same relationship is to collapse both assays into one statistic per
pair, the H3K27ac to DNase-seq ratio. If silencer-like elements are accessible but depleted of
H3K27ac, they should have a lower ratio than enhancer-like elements.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=4}
# collapse the two assays into one statistic per pair. The same pseudocount of 1 as above is used,
# which also avoids dividing by zero for elements without DNase-seq signal
enh_signal <- mutate(enh_signal, h3k27ac_dnase_ratio = (h3k27ac + 1) / (dnase + 1))

# test whether silencer-like pairs have a lower ratio than enhancer-like pairs
ratio_test <- wilcox.test(h3k27ac_dnase_ratio ~ int_class, data = enh_signal)

# plot ratio per interaction class
ggplot(enh_signal, aes(x = int_class, y = h3k27ac_dnase_ratio, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "H3K27ac / DNase-seq ratio",
       subtitle = paste("Wilcoxon p =", format.pval(ratio_test$p.value, digits = 2)),
       x = "Interaction class", y = "H3K27ac / DNase-seq (FC over control + 1)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Silencer-like pairs indeed have a roughly two-fold lower H3K27ac/DNase-seq ratio than
enhancer-like pairs (medians of
`r round(median(filter(enh_signal, int_class == "silencer")$h3k27ac_dnase_ratio), digits = 2)` vs.
`r round(median(filter(enh_signal, int_class == "enhancer")$h3k27ac_dnase_ratio), digits = 2)`).
This is in the direction expected for real silencers, which should be accessible but relatively
depleted of H3K27ac, rather than for false positives that aren't CREs at all. Note however that
this rests on only `r sum(enh_signal$int_class == "silencer")` silencer-like pairs, so this should
be treated as suggestive rather than conclusive.

Since CRISPRi doesn't distinguish between enhancers and other cis-regulatory elements, it's
possible, that some of these elements that look like silencers are CTCF sites, which can impact gene
regulation, but through other mechanisms (3D architecture).Let's compare at CTCF signal at enhancer-
and silencer-like elements compared to DNase accessibility and H3K27ac signal.
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=9}
# scatter plot of one assay against CTCF signal at the perturbed elements
ctcf_scatter <- function(signal, label) {
  ggplot(enh_signal, aes(x = ctcf + 1, y = .data[[signal]] + 1, color = int_class)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm",se = FALSE, color = "black") +
    labs(title = paste(label, "vs. CTCF"), x = "CTCF (FC over control + 1)",
         y = paste0(label, " (FC over control + 1)"), color = "Interaction class") +
    scale_color_manual(values = class_colors) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme_classic()
}

p_ctcf_dnase <- ctcf_scatter("dnase", "DNase-seq")
p_ctcf_h3k27ac <- ctcf_scatter("h3k27ac", "H3K27ac")

# arrange into one figure with a shared legend
plot_grid(p_ctcf_dnase + theme(legend.position = "none"),
          p_ctcf_h3k27ac + theme(legend.position = "none"),
          get_legend(p_ctcf_dnase), nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1, 0.4))
```

CTCF signal seems slightly positively correlated with DNase accessibility and vaguely negatively
correlated with H3K27ac. This is in line with the idea that DNase + H3K27ac marks enhancers, while
DNase + CTCF (+ low H3K27ac) represents CTCF sites that do not act as enhancers.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
# add CTCF ratios, using the same pseudocount as above
enh_signal <- enh_signal %>%
  mutate(ctcf_dnase_ratio = (ctcf + 1) / (dnase + 1),
         ctcf_h3k27ac_ratio = (ctcf + 1) / (h3k27ac + 1))

# boxplot of one ratio per interaction class, testing the two classes against each other
ratio_boxplot <- function(ratio, label) {
  ratio_test <- wilcox.test(reformulate("int_class", ratio), data = enh_signal)
  ggplot(enh_signal, aes(x = int_class, y = .data[[ratio]], fill = int_class)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
    labs(title = label, subtitle = paste("Wilcoxon p =", format.pval(ratio_test$p.value, digits = 2)),
         x = "Interaction class", y = paste(label, "(FC over control + 1)")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

# arrange both ratios into one figure
plot_grid(ratio_boxplot("ctcf_dnase_ratio", "CTCF / DNase-seq"),
          ratio_boxplot("ctcf_h3k27ac_ratio", "CTCF / H3K27ac"), nrow = 1)
```
Indeed, silencer-like elements have a higher CTCF/H3K27ac ratio as expected if these elements would
be enriched for CTCF sites
(Wilcoxon p = `r format.pval(wilcox.test(ctcf ~ int_class, data = enh_signal)$p.value, digits = 2)`).
But as before, this data is noisy and on based on a small number of silencer-like elements.

To get a more qualitative view, let's overlap elements with CTCF peaks from the same experiment and
see if silencer-like elements more often contain CTCF sites than enhancer-like elements.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=4}
# ENCODE CTCF peaks bed file
ctcf_peaks_file <- "https://www.encodeproject.org/files/ENCFF951RPD/@@download/ENCFF951RPD.bed.gz"

# load CTCF peaks
ctcf_peaks <- import(ctcf_peaks_file, format = "narrowPeak")

# get coordinates of the perturbed element of each pair
elements_gr <- sig_distal_hits %>%
  select(pair_uid, int_class, chr = pert_chr, start = pert_start, end = pert_end) %>%
  makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE, starts.in.df.are.0based = TRUE)

# record for each pair whether its element contains a CTCF peak
elements_ctcf <- sig_distal_hits %>%
  select(pair_uid, int_class) %>%
  mutate(ctcf_peak = overlapsAny(elements_gr, ctcf_peaks))

# test whether silencer-like elements more often contain a CTCF peak
ctcf_peak_test <- fisher.test(table(elements_ctcf$int_class, elements_ctcf$ctcf_peak))

# calculate proportion of elements overlapping a CTCF peak per interaction class
prop_ctcf_peak <- elements_ctcf %>%
  group_by(int_class) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), n_ctcf = sum(ctcf_peak), prop = n_ctcf / n)

# plot proportion of elements overlapping a CTCF peak
ggplot(prop_ctcf_peak, aes(x = int_class, y = prop, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_ctcf, "/", n)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Elements overlapping a CTCF peak",
       subtitle = paste("Fisher's exact p =",
                        format.pval(ctcf_peak_test$p.value, digits = 2)),
       x = "Interaction class", y = "Proportion of elements with CTCF peak") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1)),
                     limits = c(0, 0.35)) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

`r round(filter(prop_ctcf_peak, int_class == "silencer")$prop * 100, digits = 1)`% of silencer-like
elements contain a CTCF peak, compared to
`r round(filter(prop_ctcf_peak, int_class == "enhancer")$prop * 100, digits = 1)`% of enhancer-like
elements (odds ratio `r round(ctcf_peak_test$estimate, digits = 2)`). This goes in the same
direction as the signal-based ratios above, but the enrichment is not significant and the
confidence interval is wide
(`r paste(round(ctcf_peak_test$conf.int, digits = 2), collapse = "-")`), which is expected with
only `r filter(prop_ctcf_peak, int_class == "silencer")$n` silencer-like pairs. So this is
consistent with a subset of silencer-like elements being CTCF sites rather than technical false
positives, but the current data are too underpowered to establish it.

### Target and nearest gene expression levels
Next, we compare TPM level of the target genes between silencer- and enhancer-like interactions.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
ggplot(sig_distal_hits, aes(x = int_class, y = gene_tpm, fill = int_class)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
  labs(x = "Interaction class", y = "TPM", title = "Target gene TPM") +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Target genes of silencer-like interaction aren't lower than these of enhancer-like interactions.
This can have many reasons, including statistical power to detect significant effects, but doesn't
point to silencer effects. Although genes can have a mix of regulatory elements and even highly
expressed genes might have silencing distal regulatory inputs (see super enhancers, which contain
both silencing and activating TF motifs).

Lastly, let's compare expression levels of nearest genes between silencer and enhancer-like
interactions.

```{r}
# load TPM quantifications for all genes
tpm <- fread(snakemake@input$gene_tpm)

# load genome annotations and extract all gene bodies
annot <- import(snakemake@input$annot, format = "gtf")
genes <- annot[annot$type == "gene"]

# only retain annotations of genes also in TPM table, i.e. that were in DGE data
genes$gene_id <- sub("\\..+", "", genes$gene_id)  # strip version from Ensembl gene id 
genes <- genes[genes$gene_id %in% tpm$gene_id]

# add TPM values to gene annotations
mcols(genes) <- merge(mcols(genes), select(tpm, gene_id, tpm), by = "gene_id")

# infer TSS coordinates
tss <- promoters(genes, upstream = 0, downstream = 1)

# get all unique significant elements
cres <- sig_distal_hits %>% 
  select(grna_target, chr = pert_chr, start = pert_start, end = pert_end, elem_class) %>% 
  distinct()

# make genomic ranges object
cres_gr <- makeGRangesFromDataFrame(cres, keep.extra.columns = TRUE, starts.in.df.are.0based = TRUE)

# find closest gene and TSS for each CRE
nearest_genes <- nearest(cres_gr, genes)
nearest_tss <- nearest(cres_gr, tss)

# add TPM of nearest genes and TSSs to CREs table
cres <- cres %>% 
  mutate(tpm_nearest_gene = genes[nearest_genes]$tpm) %>% 
  mutate(tpm_nearest_tss = tss[nearest_tss]$tpm)

# convert to long format for plots
cres <- cres %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c("tpm_nearest_gene", "tpm_nearest_tss"), names_to = "measurement",
               values_to = "tpm")
```

```{r}
# plot nearest gene or TSS TPM values
ggplot(cres, aes(x = elem_class, y = tpm, fill = elem_class)) +
  facet_wrap(~ measurement, scales = "free") +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
  labs(x = "Interaction class", y = "TPM", title = "Nearest gene TPM") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.background = element_blank())
```

Again, no clear difference here.
